name: 中村藤吉本店 銀座店
address_ja: 〒104-0061 東京都中央区銀座6-10-1 GINZA SIX 4F
cuisine: The Uji tea house's Ginza tea room: a bowl of thin green cha-soba under a slab of fried tofu in clear dashi, then the matcha desserts people actually queue for — 生茶ゼリイ ¥1,430, まるとパフェ ¥1,485, the Ginza-only 別製まるとパフェ ¥2,200 and 宇治きん氷[抹茶] ¥1,980. Roughly ¥1,000–¥3,000 a head
neighborhood: Ginza 6-chōme, 4th floor of GINZA SIX — 2 min (222 m) from Ginza Station exit A3 (Ginza / Marunouchi / Hibiya lines)
hours_raw: 10:30〜20:30（カフェ L.O.19:30／食べログ掲載は L.O.19:45）・茶舗も10:30〜20:30。営業時間、休館日はGINZA SIXに準じます。予約不可
gf_detail: Not workable. 茶そば is a wheat-flour noodle with matcha kneaded into the dough — it is not buckwheat-only and is not gluten-free in any preparation — and its tsuyu is ordinary wheat soy sauce with dashi. The company does publish per-store allergen charts covering all six restaurant locations including Ginza, which is more than most Japanese tea houses do, but the same page states 「他のメニューと同一の厨房、共通の調理器具や食器で調理、提供をしております」 and 「アレルゲンが完全に除去されるわけではございません」 — shared kitchen, shared utensils, no removal guarantee. The dessert side is built on castella-type baked goods and wafers. Nothing here is safe for a celiac; a pot of tea is.
vegan_detail: The cha-soba is served in a bonito dashi broth; the parfaits and kakigōri are built on dairy ice cream and cream, and the house baked goods (うじていら, マルトベイク) are egg-and-butter. A plain pot of tea is of course vegan, and tea is the whole point of the place — but as a meal or a dessert stop this is not a vegan destination and nothing on the menu is labelled as such.

roles: 株式会社中村藤吉本店 — Uji tea merchant, founded 1854
chef_bio.origin: Uji, Kyoto — the house has stood on the same plot since its founding
chef_bio.background: 中村藤吉本店 is not a Tokyo restaurant that happens to sell tea; it is a 170-year-old Uji tea merchant that opened a tea room in Ginza. The founder, 中村藤吉 (1832–1896), was the fourth child of 小中村六兵衛 and 中村トサ, and set up as a tea dealer in Uji in 1854 (安政元年). The third generation, 卯吉, was elected mayor of Uji Town in 1912. The firm incorporated in 1949 as 株式会社中村藤吉本店. Its Uji premises were taken into Uji's Important Cultural Landscape designation in February 2009 as a representative group of Meiji-period tea-merchant buildings, and the Taishō-era garden on the same grounds became a Kyoto prefectural cultural property in 2017; the Byōdōin branch occupies the surviving building of 菊屋萬碧楼, an Edo-period restaurant-inn. Nine retail locations now exist, of which Ginza (GINZA SIX 4F) and Azabudai are the two in Tokyo. The house tea, 中村茶, is a deliberately transgressive blend of seven leaf types including tencha, the raw material of matcha — sencha and gyokuro are not normally blended, and the shop's own copy frames doing it anyway as play. The Ginza room seats 50, takes no reservations, and gives every arriving guest a pot of the day's welcome tea (gyokuro, when reviewers describe it) with the hot-water flask left on the table so you pour your own.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「日本茶をたのしむ起点」 — tea first, and everything on the plate arranged to show what the leaf can do rather than to be a dessert with matcha added.
chef_bio.specialty: 生茶ゼリイ; まるとパフェ (抹茶 / ほうじ茶); the Ginza-exclusive 別製まるとパフェ made with the house's 別製 matcha; 宇治きん氷[抹茶]; and the cha-soba lunch.

anecdotes.text: Reviewers consistently describe a queue outside the shop and a row of waiting chairs along the wall behind it — arriving before noon at a weekend is the difference between sitting straight down and standing in line.

A 2025 diner's account of the Ginza cha-soba: thin noodles with real buckwheat-and-matcha aroma under one large piece of fried tofu with mitsuba, in a restrained dashi — filling enough that she skipped dessert and vowed to come back for it.
The 別製まるとパフェ at ¥2,200 exists only at Ginza and is made with a matcha the house grades 別製 — the same conceit as the Uji main store's tiered parfaits, but with a grade not sold at the other branches.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: tokichi.jp's Ginza store page gives the address 〒104-0061 東京都中央区銀座6丁目10-1 GINZA SIX 4F, the phone 03-6264-5168, and 10:30–20:30 for both tea shop and café with L.O. 19:30, hours following GINZA SIX. tokichi.jp/pages/menu-allergens publishes per-store allergen charts for six locations including Ginza and states the shared-kitchen caveat verbatim. tokichi.jp/pages/history gives 1854, the founder's dates, the 1912 mayoralty, the 1949 incorporation and the 2009/2017 heritage designations. Tabelog 13207589 confirms the address, 03-6264-5168, 10:30–20:30 L.O.19:45, 予約不可, 50 seats, no private rooms, cards/e-money/QR accepted, and a 3.45 rating over 987 reviews with dessert prices.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The company's own allergen page states that dishes are cooked and served 「他のメニューと同一の厨房、共通の調理器具や食器で」 and that 「アレルゲンが完全に除去されるわけではございません」 — one kitchen, shared utensils, no removal guarantee.
茶そば is wheat-flour noodle dough with matcha worked into it, boiled in the same water as everything else on the noodle side.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard wheat shōyu assumed in the soba tsuyu; no tamari or gluten-free seasoning is mentioned anywhere on the site.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The cha-soba is served in bonito dashi; parfaits and kakigōri use dairy ice cream and cream; the baked goods are egg-and-butter.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Per-store allergen charts are published for all six restaurant locations including Ginza, and a customer line (0120-137-555, 10:00–17:00, closed Sundays) is given for allergen questions. The charts are images rather than text, so they must be read on the page.

positives.text: Published, store-specific allergen information and an honest cross-contact disclaimer — the shop tells you what it cannot promise instead of implying safety.

cultural_comfort.note: A department-store tea room on the 4th floor of GINZA SIX, two minutes from Ginza Station exit A3. No reservations, so expect a queue at weekends and around 3 pm; the wait is managed with chairs outside the door. Fifty seats, an English-friendly retail environment, cards, e-money and QR payment accepted, a photo menu, and a welcome pot of tea brought to the table with the flask left beside it so you pour your own. If you keep gluten out, treat this as a tea-only stop — order a pot and skip the food.

name: 築地すし鮮 総本店
address_ja: 〒104-0045 東京都中央区築地1-9-6 アロア築地ビル1F
cuisine: A 78-seat Tsukiji sushi-and-sake house that buys whole bluefin over 150 kg and runs from late morning until five in the morning — a ¥1,848 nigiri set at lunch, courses at ¥5,500 / ¥9,680 / ¥13,200 at night, and thirty-odd sake plus Japanese wine alongside
neighborhood: Tsukiji 1-chōme, on the Shintomicho side of the district — 3 min from Tsukiji (Hibiya line, exit 4), 5 min from Shintomichō (Yūrakuchō line, exit 4), and walkable from Higashi-Ginza
gf_detail: Nothing gluten-related is published — no allergen chart, no gluten-free claim, no tamari. Assume the table soy sauce is ordinary wheat shōyu, and that the nikiri brushed on the nigiri, the anago and unagi tare, and the tamago (mirin and shōyu) all carry wheat. The kitchen also sends out 一品料理 alongside the sushi, which in a house of this type means fried items in the same oil. Plain sashimi with your own soy sauce is the only route a celiac could take here, and it needs to be negotiated at the counter in Japanese.
vegan_detail: Not published either way. A sushi counter can always make kappa-maki and will usually have inari, but this is a tuna house: the courses are fish from first plate to last, the miso soup will be bonito dashi, and the tamago is egg. Nothing on the site is labelled vegetarian or vegan. Treat it as a place a vegan can sit at with a companion, not a place to eat a meal.

roles: operated by 株式会社クプロ (Cpro Co., Ltd.), 福岡市博多区神屋町3-26
chef_bio.origin: Tsukiji 1-chōme — the flagship of a small Fukuoka-run group
chef_bio.background: 築地すし鮮 is the core brand of 株式会社クプロ, a Fukuoka company headquartered at 福岡市博多区神屋町3-26 which runs four restaurant brands across roughly seven outlets — 築地すし鮮 itself, 出前や鮮吉 (delivery sushi), 天ぷら・寿司 博多 春宵, and the ramen shop 鳳凛 — alongside a fitness business. Under the すし鮮 name the group operates the Tsukiji 総本店, a 福岡総本店, a 4丁目場外市場店 in the Tsukiji outer market, plus 浅草雷門店, 恵比寿東口店 and 西中洲店. The Tsukiji 総本店 is the one this record belongs to and is the group's showpiece: its whole selling point is buying a bluefin tuna of 150 kg and up in one piece and cutting it in the shop, which is why the fatty cuts are the thing reviewers write about and why a ¥1,848 lunch set gets called extraordinary value in a district where lunch sushi routinely runs double that. No individual itamae is named publicly; the company's copy talks about 職人 in the plural and about 日本の食文化の真髄 rather than about a personality. The 11:00-to-5 a.m. licence is the other distinguishing fact — this is one of the very few places in Tsukiji where you can eat proper sushi at three in the morning, and the room seats 78, so it functions as much as a late-night drinking house as a sushi counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: One whole tuna, cut in-house, sold from lunchtime to dawn.
chef_bio.specialty: 本まぐろ from a single 150 kg-plus fish; the ¥1,848 lunch nigiri set; おすすめ彩コース ¥5,500 (7 dishes, walk-ins accepted), 月コース ¥9,680 (6 dishes), 雪コース ¥13,200 (7 dishes); 30-plus sake and Japanese wines.

anecdotes.text: The shop's own copy leads on the whole-fish purchase — 「一本買い」 of a bluefin over 150 kg — rather than on a chef's name; the tuna, not the itamae, is the brand.
Reviewers single out the ¥1,848 lunch nigiri set as exceptional value for Tsukiji, which is what fills the 78 seats in the middle of the day.
The kitchen runs to 4:30 a.m. last order, 365 days a year — an unusual licence for a sushi house and the reason the room turns into a late drinking spot after the market crowd has gone.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: tsukijisushisen-souhonten.com gives the address 〒104-0045 東京都中央区築地1-9-6 アロア築地ビル1F, 11:00–05:00 (L.O. 04:30), 無休, courses from ¥5,500 and ¥9,680, a ¥550 per-person otoshi and a fully non-smoking room. Tabelog 13029445 confirms the same address, the Hibiya-line Tsukiji exit-4 3-minute and Shintomichō exit-4 5-minute walks, genre 寿司・海鮮・居酒屋, 78 seats, lunch ¥1,000–1,999 / dinner ¥5,000–5,999, the ¥1,848 lunch set and the ¥13,200 雪コース, with a 3.09 rating over 183 reviews, and gives the coordinates used here. cpro-group.com's company page identifies the operator, its Fukuoka address, its four brands and its outlet counts; hotpepper.jp/gstr00545 lists the six すし鮮 branches.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen information of any kind is published — no chart, no statement, no gluten-free claim. A 78-seat izakaya-style kitchen sending out fried 一品料理 alongside the sushi.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Ordinary wheat shōyu must be assumed: no tamari or gluten-free seasoning is mentioned anywhere, and the nikiri, anago/unagi tare and tamago seasoning are all shōyu-based by default.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The courses are fish throughout and the miso soup will be bonito dashi; nothing on the menu is marked vegetarian or vegan.

cultural_comfort.note: Easy to walk into — a large ground-floor room three minutes from Tsukiji station exit 4, open every day from 11:00 to 5:00 a.m., fully non-smoking, with a photographed course menu and online booking. Two things to know: a ¥550 per-person otoshi (a compulsory appetiser charge) is added at dinner, which surprises visitors who read it as a cover charge; and if you have a wheat allergy you will need Japanese to work through the soy sauce, the nikiri and the tare with the counter, because none of it is written down.

chef_bio.background: 築地食堂 源ちゃん is not an independent Tsukiji restaurant; it is the flagship brand of 株式会社サイプレス, a company that began in 1993 with a kushiage shop called 串えもん and has opened continuously since, reaching 126 outlets across 36 brands by 2025 — 64 openings and a net gain of 37 stores since the pandemic. All outlets are directly operated rather than franchised, and the group spans washoku, conveyor sushi, western, noodle and café formats from Hokkaidō to Kyūshū. The 源ちゃん format is a market canteen: fish sourced through Toyosu and direct-from-producer routes, served as teishoku and donburi, with each outlet given slightly different menu and interior so the chain does not read as one. There is a spin-off counter format, スタンド源ちゃん. Crucially for this record, the chain's own store index lists no branch anywhere in 築地 — the Tokyo outlets are 五反田TOC, 汐留シティセンター, 新宿御苑, 新宿NSビル, 深川ギャザリア, 神保町, 晴海トリトン, 東京オペラシティ, 池袋サンシャインシティ, 飯田橋, 品川シーズンテラス, TFT有明, 有明ガーデン, 両国江戸NOREN, 大井競馬場 and アクアシティお台場 — and the only one in Chūō-ku is 晴海トリトン店 at 中央区晴海1-8-16. The 築地 in the name is heritage branding for a market the company no longer buys at; its own strapline now reads 「豊洲市場と産直ルートから」.

name: 並木藪蕎麦
cuisine: The Asakusa house of the Yabu lineage, open since 1913: a small ¥850 zaru you dip only the tip of, because the tsuyu is famously black and salty — then nori-kake ¥1,100–1,300, ten-zaru ¥2,000–2,300 and winter kamo-nanban ¥2,100, eaten standing on a warm flask of sake
neighborhood: Kaminarimon 2-chōme, one street back from Kaminarimon gate — 1 min (172 m) from Asakusa Station exits A4/A5 (Ginza line, Toei Asakusa line), 5 min from the Tōbu Isesaki line terminus
hours_raw: 月・火・金・土・日 11:00〜19:30（L.O.19:00）／水・木 定休日。予約不可。全席禁煙。カード可（VISA・Master・JCB・AMEX）、交通系電子マネー・nanaco・WAON可、QRコード決済不可
gf_detail: Not workable, and not close. Yabu-school soba is a wheat-blended dough, the boards are dusted with 打ち粉 (wheat flour), and the tsuyu this shop is actually famous for is a very dark, very concentrated wheat soy sauce — the whole point of the house style. Half the menu is tempura (天ざる, 天ぷらそば, 天ぷら ¥1,700) fried in the same small kitchen. No allergen information is published and nothing gluten-free is claimed. Even the plain zaru cannot be made safe here.
vegan_detail: The tsuyu is a bonito-and-shōyu kaeshi — there is no version of eating soba here without it — and the 玉子とじ and 花巻 are egg and dashi. Of the cold sides, 焼きのり (¥850) and わさび芋 (¥850, grated yam) are plant-based in themselves, but 板わさ is fish kamaboko and everything is served alongside the same dashi. This is not a place to eat a vegan meal.

roles: member house of 藪睦会 (the Yabu guild), founded 1913
chef_bio.origin: Kaminarimon, Asakusa — a free-standing house one street off the Kaminarimon gate
chef_bio.background: 並木藪蕎麦 opened in 1913 and is one of the three houses usually named as the 藪御三家 alongside かんだやぶそば in Kanda-Awajichō and 池の端藪蕎麦 in Yushima — all three appear on the membership roll of 藪睦会, the Yabu guild, which lists 並木藪蕎麦 at 台東区雷門2-11-9, tel. 03-3841-1340. The guild's own account of the lineage traces it to 蔦屋, a shop at 根津団子坂 in the closing years of the Edo period; the name やぶそば is said to come from the district being called 薮下, and the 蔦屋 signboard passed to 神田やぶそば, around which the guild formed more than eighty years ago. What makes Namiki its own thing rather than a branch is the tsuyu. The shop's own line is 「濃い汁の 老舗の味に 並木藪」 — a dark, salty, concentrated dip that regulars take only on the tip of the noodle, and which first-timers who plunge the whole bundle in find undrinkable. Portions are correspondingly small and large servings are not offered; the intended shape of a visit is a flask of warm sake with 板わさ, 焼きのり or わさび芋, then a fast ¥850 zaru to finish. The room is a single storey with 36 seats — two six-tops, a four-top and five four-seat raised tatami boxes — no private rooms, no reservations, no large parties. Tabelog has selected it for そば百名店 EAST in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2024 and 2025, and it holds a 3.67 average over roughly 2,600 reviews.
chef_bio.philosophy: Edo-style Yabu soba: strong dark tsuyu, small servings, sake first and noodles last.
chef_bio.specialty: ざるそば ¥850 (2023 menu); のりかけ ¥1,100 (listed at ¥1,300 on the current Tabelog display); 天ざる and 天ぷらそば ¥2,000 (¥2,300 currently); 鴨南蛮 ¥2,100, November to March only; 板わさ, 焼きのり and わさび芋 at ¥850 as sake companions.

anecdotes.text: The shop's own PR copy is a verse — 「濃い汁の 老舗の味に 並木藪」 — and goes on to describe the intended visit: warm sake, good snacks, soba to finish, 'the stylish way to eat'.
Large servings are refused: a 2025 diner recording a のりかけそば here notes 「※大盛りは不可でした」.
The 鴨南蛮 is on the menu only from November to March, printed with its own date range — a survival of the seasonal Edo practice rather than a marketing device.
The 藪睦会 roll shows how far the school spread from one Nezu shop: from かんだやぶそば and 池の端藪蕎麦 through 薮伊豆総本店 in Nihonbashi and 上野薮蕎麦総本店 out to Hachiōji, Kawagoe, Kōfu, Izu-Kōgen and Kumamoto.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: yabusoba.co.jp (藪睦会) carries the lineage account — 蔦屋 at 根津団子坂, the 薮下 etymology, the transfer of the signboard to 神田やぶそば, the guild's eighty-plus years — and its member roll gives 並木藪蕎麦 台東区雷門2-11-9 tel.03-3841-1340. Tabelog 13003650 gives the same address, 172 m from Asakusa Station with the A4/A5 exits one minute away and Tōbu five, 03-3841-1340, 予約不可, 11:00–19:30 L.O.19:00 with Wednesday and Thursday closed, 36 seats in the exact configuration quoted, all non-smoking, no parking, オープン日 1913年, budget ¥1,000–1,999 both services, the 百名店 selections and the 15-item March 2023 menu with prices. Its map page supplied the coordinates.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 36-seat house kitchen running tempura (天ざる, 天ぷらそば, 天ぷら ¥1,700) alongside the noodle boards; wheat 打ち粉 is standard on Yabu-school boards and no wheat-free handling is claimed anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The house is known specifically for an unusually dark and concentrated wheat-soy tsuyu — 「濃い汁の 老舗の味に 並木藪」 is the shop's own line. There is no tamari version and no way to eat the soba without it.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The tsuyu is bonito dashi; 玉子とじ and 花巻 involve egg and dashi; 板わさ is fish kamaboko. Only 焼きのり and わさび芋 are plant-based on their own.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, quiet, old room a minute from Kaminarimon, and it runs on unwritten etiquette rather than on English. No reservations and no large parties — turn up, wait, sit where you are put. Dip only the last inch of the noodles in the tsuyu; it is meant to be that strong. Large servings are refused, so order a side and a flask of sake if you want a full meal. Cards and Suica are fine but QR payment is not, and the shop is closed Wednesdays and Thursdays, which catches a lot of visitors out. Photograph-light menu, so knowing 「ざる」「天ざる」「のりかけ」 helps.
